text:
anya: quick mobile UX review — on small widths the dashboard cards compress ok but when the main table overflows there's a janky jump if you open the left rail. attaching screenshot, happens on iPhone 12 mini.

jordan: saw this, thanks. is the jump from layout reflow or a scroll-to-top when nav opens? any repro steps?

anya: i can repro by: 1) open project dashboard, 2) scroll table horizontally a bit, 3) tap main nav icon. the table snaps and content jumps under the rail. recorded a quick video.

sam: likely a combination of overflow + focus management. current CSS uses `overflow: auto` on the cards container and we set `transform` on the rail which can trigger repaint differences across safari/chrome mobile. quick fix to try: set `position: fixed` on rail and avoid forcing reflow. example:
```css
.left-rail { position: fixed; left: 0; top: 56px; width: 280px; transform: translateX(-100%); }
.dashboard-table { overflow-x: auto; -webkit-overflow-scrolling: touch; }
```

morgan: UX question — when the screen is narrow should we still show the rail as an overlay, or collapse it into a bottom sheet? i worry bottom sheet will cover key controls in the dashboard (filters/actions).

anya: bottom sheet covers the action bar and hides the filter chips. for accessibility I'd prefer an overlay that doesn't shift content. overlay should trap focus though.

aria-bot: accessibility scan: 1) `View` small secondary buttons fail 3:1 contrast on dark mode; 2) several interactive targets < 44px on compact cards. See rule ids: WCAG-contrast-1, WCAG-touchsize-2.

jordan: thanks @aria-bot. also we should tweak the CTA copy — `Details` is ambiguous in small spaces. propose `Open details` or `View details`? `Open details` is more action-y.

sam: another option: keep table horizontally scrollable on mobile but add an overflow fade and persistent column headers. css for gradient hint: 
```css
.table-wrap::after { content: ''; position: absolute; right: 0; width: 24px; pointer-events: none; background: linear-gradient(to left, rgba(255,255,255,1), rgba(255,255,255,0)); }
```
This avoids reflow but still communicates overflow.

anya: i'm hesitant about horizontal scroll for dense data — it's bad for discoverability. can we collapse each row into stacked key/value when width < 420px? basically transform table rows into cards with label/value pairs. more accessible and easier to tap.

morgan: prioritization: make row->stacked view P0 for onboarding and billing flows, P1 for activity logs. we shouldn't block release for generic admin pages.

sam: noted — performance caveat: converting large tables to stacked rows will defeat virtualization; we should lazy-render visible rows and keep virtualization wrappers. i'll prototype an approach that toggles rendering mode based on row count.

anya: perfect. action items: @sam prototype stacked-row variant + overlay rail (no content shift) by EOD Wed; @jordan update small-button copy to `Open details`; @morgan confirm P0 pages list; @aria-bot re-run contrast/tap target checks after CSS adjustments. thanks all :thumbsup:
